items.title: Robert Glasper interviewed by Greg Thomas, Clinton, New York, February 20, 2016
items.q: I wanted to sound like Oscar Peterson. I loved Oscar Peterson.

ctx.x: They have to tell you you have a sound because you don’t really realize you have a sound until somebody tells you. Then you go, “oh snap. Maybe I do have a sound.” You know. But other than that it’s like, “oh, I do.” You know, and then you start realizing, like I started realizing through the years people were saying, “your compositions are different. They’re kind of not like” blah-blah-blah-blah, “they kind of have this feel to it.” And I realized what I did is, you know I grew up in church and I never ignored…

right.” [sings] “I’m every woman.” You know. So I grew up with all these sounds, and going to rehearsals and everything, and so when I got into jazz and I pretty much got in and really starting like delving into jazz when I was in ninth grade or maybe eighth grade. And when I got into that, you know, what I did was I learned how to play it authentically, because I wanted to sound like Oscar Peterson. I loved Oscar Peterson. My mom used to play him in the house all the time. So I used to try my best to sound like…
